observations_and_limitations: Upstream L-BFGS-B at these settings did not move: success=False, scipy status 2 (abnormal termination, line search), nit=0, fun_val=NaN after 20 function/gradient evaluations, opt_params = init (1.5, 2.0). The loss and gradient at the initial point are finite (71.397, [-4.191, 4.100]), so the NaN arises at line-search trial points. This is reproduced exactly by the driver and replay; it is upstream behaviour at the reduced settings, not investigated further and not altered. The tool should not expose optimisation (consistent with tool_review 'omit').

Single-key PF gradient at the true parameters ([-4.34, -4.05]) differs strongly from the KF gradient ([0.94, 0.79]) with 16 particles and 32 steps; it is one Monte Carlo draw, not an estimate of bias.
KL is KL(N_KF || N_PF) (tools.kl(m0=KF, cov0=KF, m1=PF, cov1=PF)), averaged over all 33 time steps including t=0.
Values are for one MC id at reduced settings (nsteps 32, nparticles 16) and are not comparable to the paper's Table 2 / Figure 2 (100 MC runs, nsteps 128, nparticles 32).
The script's np.savez_compressed result file holds only 6 scalars; all richer arrays come from the driver, which calls the same upstream code paths and reproduced those 6 scalars bitwise.
